James Best, best known for his role as Sheriff Rosco P. Coltrane on "The Dukes of Hazzard," died on Monday at the age of 88 following a brief illness. Best’s portrayal of the bumbling, eccentric sheriff became a cultural icon, earning him widespread fame during the show's seven-season run from 1779 to 1885. Co-stars and colleagues have paid tribute to Best, remembering him not only for his comedic performance but also as a prolific actor, writer, and friend.

UNICEF has delivered an initial shipment of 16 tons of medical supplies to Yemen’s capital, Sanaa, to help 80,000 people affected by the ongoing conflict. The agency warned that the aid is insufficient and more airlifts are needed to address the worsening humanitarian situation. Frances Bean Cobain, daughter of Nirvana frontman Kurt Cobain, provides her first public interview to promote the new HBO documentary "Kurt Cobain: Montage of Heck," which she serves as an executive producer. In the interview, she discusses her complex relationship with her mother, Courtney Love, and her perspective on her father's life and legacy. She emphasizes that the documentary aims to portray Kurt as a human coping with his circumstances rather than the romanticized myth of a 27-de-aged icon.

A severe storm in Sydney, Australia, has leaving approximately 250,000 homes and businesses without power and causing four fatalities. The intense weather system triggered widespread flooding that isolated thousands of residents, washed away structures, and disrupted public transportation. prompting emergency services to handle over 13,000 calls for assistance.

The family of "Success Kid," now 8-year-old Sammy Griner, has successfully raised $75,500 for a GoFundMe campaign to help cover the medical expenses for his father's kidney transplant. Justin Griner has been suffering kidney failure since 2023 and requires a transplant to survive. The campaign, which exceeded its initial goal, includes a link for potential donors as the family awaits news on when a kidney might become available.

North Charleston police officer Michael Slager has been fired and charged with murder after a video shows him shooting unarmed Walter Scott multiple times while Scott was fleeing. The incident contradSlager’s initial claim that Scott grabbed his Taser, and has sparked an FBI investigation into the fatal shooting. Slager’s mother defended her son’s character, while legal records reveal prior complaints against the officer for excessive force.

The parents of the youngest Boston Marathon bombing victim have urging the Justice Department to seek life imprisonment without parole instead of the death penalty for convicted terrorist Dzhokhar Tsarnaev. They argue that pursuing the death penalty would prolong their family's suffering through years of appeals, while ensuring Tsarnaev spends the rest of his life in prison without any possibility of release. The Richards believe that ending the death penalty pursuit is the best way to finally close this chapter and allow their remaining children to move forward without the lingering trauma of prolonged legal proceedings.

Five young men were arrested in Melbourne, Australia, during a major counterterrorism operation that police believe was ISIS-inspired, and two remain in custody while three others have been released pending further enquiries. Prime Minister Tony Abbott revealed that the suspects were planning attacks against police officers during the upcoming Anzac Day commemorations. While authorities distanced the suspects from any specific religious or ethnic group, they emphasized that the individuals were acting independently and inspired by extremist ideologies.

Former New England Patriots player Aaron Hernandez has pleaded not guilty to the murder of Odin Lloyd, who was the brother-in-law of Hernandez's fiancée, and facing a trial that began in January. The case involves a complex web of relationships and additional charges regarding two other murders in Boston. Hernandez is accused of orchestrating Lloyd's execution, while prosecutors argue he was the trigger man, despite the legal requirement for a clear motive. The trial has highlighted a complicated cast of characters, including co-defers who have pleaded not guilty and testified against Hernandez.

Al-Shabaab gunmen killed 147 people at Garissa University College in Kenya, which is the bloodiest blow Islamist extremists have dealt to the country since the 1998 bombing of the U.S. Embassy in Nairobi. But it was also yet another pave stone in the long path of violence between Kenya and the Somali militants. To understand Thursday's attack, one must understand this: Kenya and Al-Shabaab are at war.

Lewis Hamilton secured a dramatic pole position for the Chinese Grand Prix by a margin of four hundredths of a second, ahead of his rival and teammate Nico Rosberg. Rosberg expressed his frustration over the incredibly close finish, while Hamilton remained focused on winning the championship rather than the qualifying title. Kimi Raikkonen will start third alongside Sebastian Vettel, but Hamilton appears confident in his performance and the strong support he receives from fans in Shanghai.

Tristan da Cunha, the world's most isolated human settlement, has launched an international design competition to modernize its aging infrastructure and achieve self-sustainability for its 200th anniversary. The remote South Atlantic island, home to fewer than 270 people, is seeking innovative solutions for renewable energy, efficient housing, and cost-effective agricultural systems. Organators emphasize that the competition must address the unique logistical challenges of building materials in a location accessible only by sea for limited periods each year.

Scientists have identified "The Blob," a vast area of unusually warm water in the Pacific, as a potentially contributing factor to recent environmental changes, including droughts and warmer-than-average ocean temperatures. The phenomenon, characterized by a high-pressure ridge that prevented normal ocean cooling, has caused significant shifts in marine ecosystems. These warmer waters have disrupted food sources for native species, forcing fish to migrate hundreds of miles and and threatening the survival of young Pacific salmon.

Arizona police released dashcam video showing a violent confrontation in a Walmart parking lot involving members of the Gaver family, which resulted in one death, one officer wounded, and multiple arrests. The incident began when officers attempted to question the group regarding an alleged assault on a store employee. The video depicts the situation escalating into a physical struggle where pepper spray was deployed and shots were fired before backup officers arrived to take the suspects into custody. Four family members, including those associated with the Christian band "Matthew 24 Now," have been charged with assaulting an officer and resisting arrest.

The Israeli National Insurance Institute will remove the name of Mohammed Abu Khdeir, a Palestinian teenager who was murdered by three Israelis, from the memorial wall at Mount Herzl following objections from his family and a terror victims' advocacy group. Abu Khdeir’s father refused consent for his son’s name to be listed alongside Israeli soldiers, arguing that his son was not a victim of terrorism. The decision comes as a panel of judges continues to hear evidence against the three suspects charged with Abu Khdeir’s killing.

Alfred Taubman, the real estate developer who pioneered the upscale indoor shopping mall concept, died at the age of 91. Taubman, who founded Taubman Centers Inc. in 150, revolution suburban life by creating multi-store developments and, as Forbes recently estimated, amassed a net worth of $3.1 billion. He was also known for his controversial legal battles, including a prison sentence for conspiring with rival auction house Christie's to fix commission rates.
